messages.author: 4e6a4cb87be03953
messages.subject: Confidence interval for empirical ICC
parts:
Hi Phil,

I wonder if you would consider adding a confidence interval feature for empirical ICC plots returned from "itemfit" function. This type of plot exists in packages like eRm and programs such as Winsteps. However, they are either for unidimensional models or just dichotomous models. An empirical plot based on the average step values of partial credit model or other polytomous models would be a nice feature. 

Thanks,
Okan

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Confidence interval for empirical ICC
parts:
Hi Okan,

Thanks for the suggestion, but I think I've already done that for
dichotomous and ploytomous items types. It's in the examples, just
look for the lines containing the argument empirical.plot = #.

If that isn't the plot you are looking for, could you send me a
snapshot of what you are referring to. Cheers.

Phil

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Confidence interval for empirical ICC
parts:
Hi Okan,

I see what you are saying now. Yes, those aren't implemented in the
package, partially because they seems somewhat strange to me. The raw
estimates are calculated from binned empirical θ estimates, which
naturally contain some imprecision, and are subject to how much
'binning' one does with the estimated θ scores. As a consequence, so
are the error bars, which makes them doublely imprecise and hard to
interpret.

Typically these empirical estimates are used to visibly measure
goodness of fit, but with smaller sample sizes they don't perform well
at all (and with larger sample sizes there are better stats anyway,
like the S-X2). I certainly could add the error bars in to the plots,
I just wonder how useful they really are and whether over-plotting
will be an issue.

If you are only interested in how the parameter shapes might vary, I
think the more natural way to look at how the parameter space is
influenced by the model information. Check out the itemplot(mod, 1, CE
= TRUE) plot to generate confidence ellipses in parameter space that
are mapped into data-space (requires an information matrix to be
computed beforehand). This should get at the same idea as the error
bars in the plots you are looking for, though personally I think they
are a bit nicer and easier to grasp. Cheers.

Phil

messages.author: 4e6a4cb87be03953
messages.subject: Re: Confidence interval for empirical ICC
parts:
Hi Phil,

Thanks a lot for your detailed response. I totally agree with you about the imprecision of error bars that are computed using raw scoring or other similar methods. I have been using Winsteps to generate those and I have also used eRm. They provide fairly different intervals for empirical ICCs because of their binning methods. Since my sample size is usually around 400 to 1000, even small changes in the algorithm makes big differences in the results. I will look at the method you suggested. I guess I better focus on statistical examination of item fit rather than using graphical illustrations.
Thanks again for your help. I really appreciate it.

Okan
